19827426.d:
Role: Field Service Installer (Contract - IMBOX Flagship DEO Upgrade)

Overview: A brief introduction to the IMBOX Flagship unit and the goal of this contract: upgrading the machine's legacy components to the new 1.5 standard.

Core Scope of Work (The 3 Key Upgrades)

Task 1: Valve Plate Upgrade (v1.0 to v1.5): Disassembling the lower technical chamber, disconnecting old pumps/wiring, performing drawer rail modifications, mounting the new v1.5 plate, and executing complex low-voltage wiring connections (WAGO junction boxes and I/O board pin configurations).

Task 2: DEO Column System Replacement: Accessing the spray chamber, dismounting internal hardware, disconnecting valves and pneumatic tubes, installing the new DEO column, routing new tubing, and setting up the DEO fluid suction canister system.

Task 3: Shoe Rack Carousel & Stepper Motor Upgrade: Replacing the old carousel with the 1.5 system. This includes removing the old stepper motor and limit switches, carefully marking left/right switch wiring, routing wires through a rubber grommet, fitting a new bearing, aligning the motor shaft, and installing a modified shoe rack.

Required Tool Kit Checklist

A consolidated, clear checklist of the exact tools the installer must bring to the site (from standard screwdrivers and specific Torx keys to socket wrenches, zip ties, and specialized items like a plastic hammer for seating bearings).

Quality Assurance & Post-Installation Testing

Guidance on how to boot up the machine, access the Service Menu (using the service passkey), and run software testing scripts ("Priming.js", "Priming DEO.js", and full diagnostic treatments) to verify the spray pattern and carousel movement before leaving the site.

Critical Technician Warnings & Best Practices

Essential guidelines for a first-time installer: wire-labeling discipline (marking left/right switches), delicate handling of stepper motor shafts and wiring, hose routing care, and safety protocols (unplugging main power).

19851657.d:
Technician Assignment Requirements

Before Accepting

- Read the Scope of Work (SOW) and Installation Guide.
- Confirm you have all required tools, materials, and software before applying.

Required Communication

- 24 Hours Prior: Confirm your assignment by calling ServicePoint or leaving a note in the WorkMarket ticket.
- Day of Service: Confirm you are still on schedule for an on-time arrival.
- Check-In: Call ServicePoint from your vehicle before entering the site to verify there are no updates.
- Mid-Point (4+ Hour Jobs): Contact Dispatch with a status update and obtain approval to continue.
- PLEASE NOTE THAT THIS IS A 4 HOUR MINIMUM JOB...IF YOU ARE REQUESTED TO STAY ONSITE AFTER (4) HOURS, YOU WILL BE COMPENSATED.
- Check-Out: Upload all required deliverables before calling Dispatch. Ensure photos are clear, sign-off sheet times match system times, and all documentation is complete. Incomplete documentation may delay payment.

Scope of Work

*(See Installation Guide in the Documents section.)*

Failure to follow the Installation Guide may result in non-billable delays.

Work includes:

- Update routers, switches, and network cabling.
- Reorganize network racks.
- Replace cash wrap/office switches (where applicable).
- Verify all devices are online with Support.
- Label and box removed equipment.
- Upload required photos, checklist, and sign-off sheet.
- Check out with Support and ServicePoint TAC.

Required Equipment

Bring the following:

- Printed and electronic copies of the Installation Guide and Sign-Off Sheet.
- Fully charged laptop with power supply, Microsoft Teams, Word, Excel, Email, PuTTY, and IP verification capability.
- Fully charged cellphone with charger, hotspot, camera, internet access, and Zoom.
- Console cable with serial adapter (USB-to-Ethernet hubs are not permitted).
- Drill (24V recommended), tap/extractor, 10' ladder, cable tester, hand tools, scissors/snips, Sharpie, label maker with extra batteries, white label tape, paperclip, Velcro cable ties, butt set/analog phone.
- Networking supplies: Cat6 patch cables, bulk Cat6 cable, RJ45 connectors, punch-down/termination tools, and biscuit jacks.

Professional Expectations

You represent ServicePoint while onsite.

- Maintain a professional appearance and customer-first attitude.
- Do not discuss pricing or payment with customers or Support.
- Do not bring unauthorized personnel onsite.
- Do not remove equipment without approval from both the client and ServicePoint.
- Failure to follow these requirements may result in removal from the project and/or loss of pay.

Dress & Safety

- No drugs, alcohol, weapons, or working under the influence.
- Wear a plain polo or button-down shirt (no logos), khaki-style pants, and hard-soled shoes.

Communication & Payment

By accepting this assignment, you agree to receive ServicePoint communications via phone, text, and email and are expected to respond promptly.

Technicians are responsible for requesting budget increases, expense reimbursements, and closing out their assignments. All reimbursement requests must be submitted within 48 hours of checkout.

Cancellation Policy

- Canceled before travel: No payment
- Canceled while enroute: $50 cancellation fee
- Site aborted after arrival: 15% of contracted flat rate (minimum $75)

19847859.d:
Onsite technician to survey, reconfigure, and validate all network printers (and time clocks where applicable) at the assigned site. Work backend-configured by remote support; technician handles physical survey, DHCP cutover, and print testing.

Tasks:

1. Check in – Meet the site contact and confirm the expected number of network printers.
2. Survey printers – For each printer: locate it, record location, MAC, IP, serial number, and model, and log all details in the Smartsheet.
3. Notify remote support – Alert the remote team once the survey is complete and wait for backend configuration to finish.
4. Convert to DHCP (one printer at a time) – Change each printer from Static IP to DHCP, restart it, verify the new IP, then refresh the PrinterLogic client on a workstation.
5. Test printing – Print a test page from a workstation and confirm the printer works before moving to the next unit.
6. Time clocks –Convert time clocks from Static IP to DHCP and verify they reconnect and function properly.

Completion criteria: All printers surveyed and logged in Smartsheet, converted to DHCP, and validated with a successful test print. Time clocks (where applicable) reconnected and confirmed working.

19673199.d:
Senior Infrastructure Engineer / Administrator — Contract (On-Site, Menlo Park, CA)

Type: Full-time contract (40 hrs/week) · 3-month minimum · Possible contract-to-hire

Location: On-site, Menlo Park, California

About the Role

A leading genomics organization is seeking a senior infrastructure engineer to fill a critical operational gap following the recent departure of a key team member. You'll maintain day-to-day operational continuity while the permanent role is filled, and help drive a major upcoming NetApp storage refresh. This is a hands-on role for someone who can operate independently in an environment with limited documentation and significant tribal knowledge to reconstruct.

What You'll Do

Handle daily operations including file restores, access and permission issues, AWS IAM requests, S3 provisioning, storage alerts and health monitoring, hardware failures (power supplies, NICs, servers), archive monitoring, and vendor support interactions. You'll also validate and build documentation as you learn the environment, and support strategic infrastructure projects — most notably an upcoming NetApp storage refresh involving new deployment, data and volume migration, mount-point remapping, and vendor coordination.

Environment

On-prem NetApp and VAST Data storage, Rocky Linux / Red Hat systems, a Slurm HPC cluster, ~100–140 GPU compute servers, several hundred VMs, SolarWinds monitoring, and OpsGenie paging. Cloud responsibilities (AWS and GCP) are limited to platform management — IAM, S3, Control Tower, and policy administration — not application workloads. Data archiving runs on Starfish with cloud-based archival storage, including weekly retrieval requests.

Must-Have Skills

The three critical skills are enterprise Linux administration, enterprise storage administration, and high-performance computing (HPC) administration. You should be comfortable troubleshooting undocumented systems and stabilizing operations quickly with minimal supervision.

Success Timeline

Week 1: environment discovery and investigation. Month 1: stabilization of operations. Months 2–3: steady-state operations plus documentation development.

Support Model

Primarily business-hours support (Pacific Time), with limited after-hours coverage, occasional pageable incidents, and scheduled maintenance windows performed after-hours or on weekends as needed.

Requirements & Compliance

No government security clearance required. Visa sponsorship (including H1B) is not available — candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S. without sponsorship for any permanent hire. Background screening will be conducted through the staffing provider.

Please send a copy of your resume to Richard.Cortez@Suryl.com

Technician will perform a Back Office PC (BOPC) refresh at a Customer retail location during an approved after-hours service window.

Important: This project includes removal and return of legacy equipment. - Before leaving site, technicians must verify:
- All personnel have exited the location.
- All doors and windows are secured.

Installing the Sunshade:

-Sunshade:

*PDF for Sunshade Installation for technician*

<https://drive.google.com/file/d/14kVOu1gIiY99LHSp7UpFzKjW8YRTY1V-/view?usp=sharing>

- Tape the top of the control bay door with painter’s masking tape.
- Center the sunscreen bracket’s back plate on the masked area of the control bay door.
- Hold the backplate firmly in place as it was measured in step two and mark the four holes using a sharpie pen.
- Carefully drill the holes with a 5/32 drill bit.
- Assemble the front bracket, sunscreen shade and the backing plate in that order.
- Use the adhesive sealant RTV silicone, fill in each of the four holes that were drilled.
- Install the assembled sunscreen with the brackets and the four screws in place onto the control bay door.
- Run a thin bead of RTV silicone on top of the sunscreen bracket, in order to ensure that no moisture will penetrate from the top.

Regular Lockers Decal Replace:

- Use a heat gun to heat the old decal, so it's easier to remove.
- Use soapy water to clean the debris on the Lockers, then finish with rubbing alcohol spray to wash off the soapy water residue.
- Align the decals and use magnets to hold them into place, then slowly peel the decals.
- Stick in the decals using a squeegee, removing air bubbles along the way.
- Cut the decal accordingly, and verify none are peeling.

Replace and Install New Decals:

- Use a heat gun to heat the old decal, so it's easier to remove.
- Use soapy water to clean the debris on the Lockers, then finish with rubbing alcohol spray to wash off the soapy water residue.
- Align the decals and use magnets to hold them into place, then slowly peel the decals.
- Stick in the decals using a squeegee, removing air bubbles along the way.
- Cut the decal accordingly, and verify none are peeling.

Tips:

- Use a heat gun to assist with removing and applying the decals.
- Surface must be clean and dry before placing decals. Make sure you have wiped down decal placement areas with 70% rubbing alcohol before setting. • Measure and level first before placing decals.
- NOTE: Do not use higher concentration alcohols as they can wear off the powercoat and negatively impact decal adhesion.
- You can use painters tape to mark locations measured. Magnets can be used to hold decals in place while you measure, check level, and step back to get a clearer perspective on symmetry. You can only place once!

Scope of Work

Phase 1 - Onsite Arrival and Preparation

Upon arrival, the ServicePoint technician will:

Check in with designated site personnel.

Establish communication with Deutsche Telekom Competency Center engineers.

Join a live support session utilizing Microsoft Teams (preferred) or Cisco WebEx.

Verify access to network equipment and required work areas.

Confirm readiness for the scheduled cutover activity.

The onsite resource will join a live support session (Microsoft Teams preferred, Cisco WebEx acceptable) with Deutsche Telekom Competency Center engineers. During this session, the resource will be guided step-by-step through the following activities:

Connect a console cable to the onsite router to allow remote configuration changes

Perform a cable swap from the legacy circuit to the new circuit as directed

Assist with basic identification of network circuits and cabling

After the circuit cutover is complete, the resource will:

Validate internet connectivity via laptop or mobile device

Coordinate with onsite RWE personnel to confirm:

WiFi connectivity

Printing functionality

Access to business-critical websites and applications

Resource Requirements

The onsite technician should have:

Basic knowledge of data circuits, network hardware (routers), and cabling

Laptop with console access capability and Cisco console cable

AnyDesk installed (free trial version is sufficient)

Access to Microsoft Teams or Cisco WebEx (Teams preferred)

Cellular hotspot or phone tethering capability for backup connectivity

Mobile phone availability for communication during potential outages

Additional Notes

Activities are low complexity but require reliable communication with remote engineering teams

Onsite personnel will not be expected to perform advanced configuration independently

Required Tools/Skillset:

- Laptop w/ AC adapter and Putty Installed
- Smart Phone with ability to take photos and Hot Spot functionality
- Cisco Console Cable
- Cat5e patch cables for testing
- Basic Hand Tools
- Cat5e cable tester
- Toner and wand
- 150ft Cat5e cable
- RJ45 modular ends

Code of Conduct:

Always maintain a professional and respectful tone when communicating with customers.

All conversations should remain focused on addressing the customer's needs in a courteous and business-appropriate manner.

Personal or overly familiar interactions can lead to misunderstandings and may reflect poorly on both you and the company.

Any deviation from this standard may result in loss of pay and removal from the project.

Drug Policy/Dress Code;

Do not bring illegal drugs, alcohol, or weapons onsite, and do not be under the influence while working. You must be clean, presentable, and dressed appropriately, clothing should not be torn or soiled. Appropriate dress includes plain polo or button-down shirt, khaki-style pants, and hard-soled shoes.

Technicians are responsible for requesting a budget increase or expense reimbursement as well as closing out their own assignment for payment. All budget increases or expense reimbursements must be requested within 48 hours after checking out, otherwise they will not be approved.

Do not remove, take, or ask to take, any equipment off the premises unless confirmed it is okay to do so by the client. Removing any equipment without the knowledge of the client and ServicePoint may be considered theft.

Do not discuss your pay rate or share payroll information with the customer or your co-workers. Should you have payroll issues, contact your recruiter or the payroll department directly.

Aborted sites with hourly payment terms will be paid per the terms for actual time onsite with a one hour minimum. If a site is aborted and there is a flat rate for the payment terms, the ticket will be closed out for 50% of the contracted rate, subsequent days scheduled will be considered 'Cancelled', not 'Aborted'.

All site aborts and out of scope work MUST be approved by ServicePoint.

Overview:

- Seeking a technician with experience in replacing monitors
- Tech is required to replace the monitor and wall mount in the Drive Thru for the DVR.
- Tech will need to run the new cable for the monitor.

Tools Required: *must haves*

- 8ft Ladder
- VGA and HDMI monitor or VGA to HDMI and HDMI to VGA adapter with cables.
- USB Keyboard
- Spot monitor (optional)
- Recommending tech have PPE for dust and debris

Scope of Work:

Pre-Site Requirements

1. Please do not schedule your visit on weekends and during meal rushes. Envysion Support Center hours are 6:00 AM - 8:00 PM Mountain Time week days and 8am-4:30pm on weekends.
2. If you go on the weekend without permission, you may have to return if the issue is not resolved, and you will not get a return bonus
3. Call the site to introduce yourself and let them know you are on your way.
4. Phone numbers are listed on Google Maps
5. If there is an issue with the time window please let us know by messaging the work order manager or calling the support number for emergency. Envysion Support (877) 258-9441 Option 2, Option 2 again, and the Option 5 would be for the field nation callers

On-Site Tasks

1. Tech needs to call to check in with the Envysion Helpdesk at (877) 258-9441 Option 2, Option 2 again, and the Option 5 would be for the field nation callers
2. Introduce yourself to the manager on duty and explain you are with Envysion Support, here to work on the CCTV system
3. Replace DVR monitor.
4. If you have been onsite for over an hour and a half, you need to reach out to the helpdesk and update them with the current progress.
5. During some visits, rarely, it is possible that additional troubleshooting may be requested for CCTV cameras (This may include re-angling, removing obstructions, or resolving video quality issues) or network connections, please be prepared to encounter this if necessary.
6. If this is considered out of scope message work order manager for compensation.
7. Check out with Envysion support. Envysion Support number (877) 258-9441 Option 2, Option 2 again, and the Option 5 would be for the field nation callers
8. Leave any old equipment with the site.
9. If checking out with support please be patient as sometimes there is a big volume of calls. Voicemail will not be considered as your check out.
10. If a return visit is needed please commit to a return visit within 24 hours

Required On-Site Deliverables

1. Upload any pictures that were taken as well upload any picture of expenses if needed.
2. Check-out of work order via Field Nation and add any notes.

Dress code and behavior policy

- Remember to be respectful of site employees and Envysion support
- Do not approach site employees if there is no need to, please reach out to the manager on duty only
- If there are any issues please find a manager or call Envysion support
- Dress appropriately for work being done on site

Escalation Process:

Contact Work Order Manager via direct message for non-work related issues such as: ETA adjustments, needing to do a return trip, questions regarding pay

- If immediate assistance is needed call the support line 877-258-9441, Option 2, Option 2 again, and the Option 5 would be for the field nation callers

Additional Hours & Expenses Approval Payment Policy

1. Expenses
2. Payment for additional expenses for equipment, such as Fuses, BNC connectors, RJ45 connectors, patch cables, and silicone caulk will be paid only if a receipt is submitted in the Field Nation App and approved by the Work Order Manager.
3. Additional hours

- This is a fixed rate work order to complete the scope of work listed in the service description. There is no hourly rate if the tech goes past the times that we have estimated for completion. Any additional work completed or extenuating circumstances will be taken into consideration and adjustment may be made at the work order managers discretion. The only exception to this is if a counter offer was accepted by the work order manager

19815371.d:
(MUST HAVE STARLINK APP DOWNLOADED PRIOR TO DISPATCHING!)

Please ensure you have a Valid ID for Site Access.

Technician will survey to determine site conditions for a future Starlink Dish at a commercial location. If you are accepting this survey, you will also be required to complete the installation.

Tech needs to meet with POC, (info provided in provisioning form if provided). Tech will start the survey, take pics and DRAW/WRITE on pics. Confirm dish-to-power distance and identify if 75 ft or 150 ft Starlink cable is required for install. Make sure to take the obstruction test and obtain SIGNED CTS sign off sheet. Tech needs to fill out the excel form digitally, if it can't be done onsite, please fill it out and callback as soon as possible. DO NOT LEAVE site until the pics are approved by CTS support and bridge.

Scope of Work Steps:

- Determine site's demarc environment and conditions
- Locate proposed location for future Starlink Dish and Router
- Confirm dish-to-power distance to determine if 75 ft or 150 ft Starlink Cable is needed
- Using the Starlink app, determine the best area for signal. (The Starlink needs an unobstructed view of the sky to capture the best signal)
- Determine Roof access/requirements needed to install Starlink Dish
- Collect required information per Survey Excel Sheet and collect required photos
- PHOTOS MUST BE NEATLY MARKED UP!
- IF TRAVEL IS REQUIRED FOR THE INSTALL, PLEASE NOTATE THAT ON THE SURVEY
- Confirm deliverables and check out with Support (If not done, job will not be considered complete, and you could jeopardize payment.)

Required Tools/Materials:

- Fully Charged Smartphone w/power cord and Hot Spot
- Starlink App Downloaded on your Phone
- Fully Charged Laptop w/power supply and Console Cable
- 8-10ft ladder
- Basic Hand Tools
- Measuring Tape/Measuring Wheel

Code of Conduct:

- Always maintain a professional and respectful tone when communicating with customers.
- All conversations should remain focused on addressing the customer's needs in a courteous and business-appropriate manner.
- Personal or overly familiar interactions can lead to misunderstandings and may reflect poorly on both you and the company.
- Any deviation from this standard may result in loss of pay and removal from the project.

Drug Policy/Dress Code;

Do not bring illegal drugs, alcohol, or weapons onsite, and do not be under the influence while working. You must be clean, presentable, and dressed appropriately, clothing should not be torn or soiled. Appropriate dress includes plain polo or button-down shirt, khaki-style pants, and hard-soled shoes.

Flat rate covers up to two hours onsite. Any additional time will be paid at $40/hr. If tech requires additional amount in overtime OR travel, it MUST be approved beforehand.

Technicians are responsible for requesting a budget increase or expense reimbursement as well as closing out their own assignment for payment. All budget increases or expense reimbursements must be requested within 48 hours after checking out, otherwise they will not be approved.

Do not remove, take, or ask to take, any equipment off the premises unless confirmed it is okay to do so by the client. Removing any equipment without the knowledge of the client and ServicePoint may be considered theft.

Do not discuss your pay rate or share payroll information with the customer or your co-workers. Should you have payroll issues, contact your recruiter or the payroll department directly.

Aborted sites with hourly payment terms will be paid per the terms for actual time onsite with a one hour minimum. If a site is aborted and there is a flat rate for the payment terms, the ticket will be closed out for 50% of the contracted rate, subsequent days scheduled will be considered 'Cancelled', not 'Aborted'.

All site aborts and out of scope work MUST be approved by ServicePoint.

IMPORTANT INFORMATION:

Our insurance requires all providers dispatched to our jobsites to have Worker’s compensation coverage. If you do not provide proof of this coverage, TRCA will provide this for your site visit, and the cost (listed as a penalty charge) will be applied to all work orders. Work orders will have 1% of labor only deducted from the total pay. Note: travel or materials cost do not apply, the deduction is for labor only. If you have a COI with workers compensation, please let the work order manager know, so we can get a copy of the COI with TRCA listed as the Certificate Holder and waive this deduction. The full scope of work is in the attached document, see below for a brief synopsis:

- TECH WILL BE WORKING ON PHONES. Attached is the full documentation of installation (Installation Guide FN Techs) to this project, please READ this so you know what to expect. Keep in mind that some items may not be exact as sites may vary.
- must take before and after pictures, so please note the picture requirement in this work order
- must be familiar with analog phone lines and 66-block​, for these sites the 66 blocks are typically in the ceiling above the IT rack. Some sites vary from the standard and the current incoming phone line locations MUST be determined.
- must complete the attached "Pre-Install Checklist" and "Certificate of Installation Completion". Pictures of these must also be attached to this Work Order
- test to ensure all devices work, phones roll over correctly from 1,2.3,4, Caller ID functioning(this must be done BEFORE any work is started and AFTER all work is complete, see attached SOW for more details)
- project must be completed between 7 am to 10 am local time before the business opens.
- Here is the simplified SOW, this is a basic guide to what needs to be done while on-site...
- Locate the 66 blocks. We know that there are at least 2 blocks, but there may be more. *See the attached pictures.*
- One 66 block is above the ceiling to the left of the IT Rack
- The other block is directly next to the IT Rack.
- Tone the cable/cables from the Wall Plates that the phones are plugged into back to the 66 block.
- Remove these cables from the 66 block and label "Phone 1", "Phone 2", "Phone 3", and "Phone 4".
- Run a CAT5E cable from the 66 block location to the IT Rack.
- Make sure this wire is dropped down the wall to the IT Rack.
- Using the supplied B-connectors, splice the newly run CAT5E at the 66 block as follows...
- Blue pair on CAT5E to Phone 1 pair.
- Orange Pair on CAT5E to Phone 2 pair.
- Green Pair on CAT5E to Phone 3 pair.
- Brown pair on CAT5E to Phone 4 pair.
- Neatly dress the splice and cabling at the 66 block.
- Take pictures of the splice point and its location.
- In the IT rack strip the newly run CAT5E cable and screw the wires down to the supplied terminal strip in the same order as the pigtails.
- Using the double-sided tape on the terminal strip mount the terminal strip on the back wall of the IT Rack.
- Route one of the pigtails from the terminal strip to the ATA.
- Route the other pigtail to the CallerID box.
- Remove all connections from the CallerID and plug in the RJ11 from the pigtail in the following order.
- Line 1 - Blue Pair
- Line 2 - Orange Pair
- Line 3 - Green Pair
- Line 4 - Brown Pair
- Remove all connections from the ATA and plug in the RJ11 from the other pigtail in the same order as the CallerID.
- Manage all wiring to be neatly installed.
- Take pictures of final install and attach them to this WO.
- Call Vivant and complete the full testing of the phones.
- If labels are not installed, install labels for Phones and the wall for the Lines.
- project must be completed between 6 am to 10 am local time before the business opens. arrival time must not be later than 8 am to allow for 1 hour of installation
- must-have RJ11 ends, RJ45 ends and some cat5 cables in case needed to make a longer cat5 cable
- you must have your own 10+ foot ladder for these installations, anywhere from 8 to 20 feet working height
- must be willing to get the job complete in one trip
- must work with Vivant Tech support to test POS

Join us in making an impact! ClearCaptions is dedicated to helping customers live a more independent life by connecting them to their loved ones via a captioned phone.

Work order is located in a RESIDENTIAL SETTING with HARD-OF-HEARING and/or ELDERLY CUSTOMERS.

- Patience, empathy, and kindness are paramount.
- Thorough, hands-on customer training is imperative to the successful completion of this work order.

OVERVIEW

Before Site Visit: *Approximately 30 minutes*

- Review all work order details, execute 24-hour advance customer courtesy call/text/voicemail, re-familiarize self on installation process via guidance material.
- Phone kit will be onsite (kit does NOT include additional required tools listed).

At Site Visit: *Approximately 1.25 - 2 hours*

- Your Objective: Customer is satisfied and able to use the fully operational phone independently and confidently by the time you leave site.
- PHASE 1 - Customer Registration: *Approximately 15-30 minutes*
- Register and validate customer's identity, then unpack and set-up their phone. Be prepared to troubleshoot per attached installation guidance to ensure successful phone registration, pairing, and connectivity.
- PHASE 2 - Phone Set-up: *Approximately 15-30 minutes*
- Unpack and set-up customer's phone, in desired and effective location
- Be prepared to troubleshoot per attached installation guidance to ensure successful phone registration, pairing, and connectivity.
- PHASE 3 - Customer Training: *Approximately 45-60 minutes*
- Once customer registration, identity validation and phone installation are complete, the remainder of your visit should focus on training the customer to use their new phone with confidence and satisfaction.
- This includes but is not limited to: placing and receiving test calls, adding contacts, setting up voicemail and/or connecting their current service, configuring their settings, and connecting them to ClearCaptions for the required Welcome Call.
- Additional site-visit callouts:

%description.html%

IMPORTANT NOTES & EXPECTATIONS

Assignment:

- DO NOT send or bring any unauthorized persons to the customer's home,* including those part of a service company. Only the tech assigned to the WO is allowed onsite.

Visit Preparation:

- Review the work order details and acknowledge (in Tasks) the guidance material attached to the work order to ensure a successful visit.
- Download and reference the Installation Checklist for detailed, step-by-step set-up requirements and customer training best practice*.
- The easy to read, flip through Phone Guide for training the customer can be found here: <https://rb.gy/i4mdjy> (PDF version for print or download is Documents section of the work order.)
- Dress Code: Clean and presentable business casual attire. Slacks or jeans (no holes/patches), closed-toed shoes, and a polo shirt. No hats.

Scheduling & Arrival:

- ClearCaptions does not accept Technician requests to reschedule, as the hard start time has been coordinated with the end customer. If required for an unexpected reason, tech must Report a Problem on the work order selecting “I Can’t Make My Assignment”. This enables ClearCaptions to attempt re-assignment without impacting our customer.
- Technician must proceed to installation appointment as scheduled even if a customer does not respond to the required 24-hour advance courtesy call or their number is "disconnected".* Customers are hard or hearing so may not realize you attempted to call until they have their new phone and ClearCaptions service.
- Check-in + Check-out must be within 1 mile of site.
- You will be able to access the Customer Information when you are ON SITE and checked in*.
- Please arrive at start time of WO. Too early or too late can disrupt the customer and the ability to complete the WO. We will not approve requests to edit time logs.
- If customer is not home and not reachable after 15 min of hard start time,* to confirm if an approved Power-of-Attorney is on site, or to repo

 If this is an RMA/Warranty a form is required to be filled out. All non-TV warranties/RMA's are required to be dropped off at the shipping location before check out

An appropriate escalation path has been provided below if you cannot reach your work order manager within 15 minutes of reaching site.

Site Visit Number: 1

Number of Technicians Required: 1

Description:

Location has received a new TMAX timer for their Sauna unit, which is used to remotely trigger their tanning or massage amenities to turn on for a desired period. We need your assistance with installing the new timer & installing a line that connects this new timer to the rest of the TMAX system (daisy chain)

Support Contacts:

Work Order Manager: Matthew Dow | Phone: (860) 792-0492

Vendor: Applied Digital (TMAX Support) | Phone: 417-297-0361

Tools Needed:

Hand tools, data cable tester with RJ11 port, RJ11 connectors (male) and keystones (female), RJ22 connectors (male), data cable crimper, data cable punchdown tools, unterminated CAT6 cable

Special Note:

RJ22 connectors are non-standard, and are typically used for small connections (most commonly used to connect a wired phone’s handset to the base station). If you do not own RJ22 connectors, please discuss with your work order manager about having them procure the connectors for you, or procure them yourself and be reimbursed.

Scope of Work:

1. Call your work order manager upon arrival so they may verify your check-in.

2. Check in with management on site to ensure they are aware of your presence and work on site today.

3. Locate the package containing the new TMAX timers. Bring to the Black Card Spa.

4. Locate the existing TMAX daisy chain & determine which unit is the last in the line

5a. Either daisy chain a new line from the last unit in the line to this Sauna unit

OR

5b. Run a new line from the Sauna's room to the 2nd port on the TMAX Manager device

6. Create a new RJ-11 to RJ-22 cable to connect the new timer to the new wall jack that was just installed

7. Install TMAX timers on the TMAX lines behind the Sauna unit. Ask staff / management for verification on which amenities are the massage chairs.

8. Call Applied Digital at the number above to ensure the timers are configured properly.

9. Verify with staff / management that they are able to use the TMAX / Radianse system following the installation of the new timer.

!! If you need to reterminate a TMAX line: 4 copper lines are required for use. Make sure to take careful note of the termination order in the connector that you are replacing and follow the same order on the new termination.

!! Our standard termination order is (left to right) blue, blue stripe, orange, orange stripe, with the connector facing away from you, pin-side up.

!! Please reach out to your work order manager if you have any questions or concerns regarding TMAX line termination.

- Patience, empathy, and kindness are paramount.

Scope of Work: Cat-6 cable installation.

- Technician is to replace the network cable with a new Cat-6 cable, terminate and reconnect the camera.

Service Description – Standard AReS Fire Alarm InstallationEstimated Work Order Time:- Minimum: 1 hour
- Maximum: 2 hours
- Time can be extended with customer approval.

Project Overview:

This project involves transitioning from POTS to Wireless technology, requiring expertise in low voltage wiring, tracing, tagging, and testing.

- 1
- 2

Responsibilities:You will install a physical enclosure containing a CradlePoint router, ATA, UPS, and an attached 66-Block. All equipment is pre-activated, configured, and secured within the enclosure.

The enclosure and 66-block are typically installed on a plywood backboard in the customer's "Telco" room (MPOE). After installation, a connection from our 66-block to the application service (e.g., Fire Alarm, Burglar, Voice, Fax, Elevator, Modem) is required.

Post-installation, tests are necessary to ensure the CradlePoint equipment is active and can "call home."

Note:Only the assigned provider is authorized to complete the work. Technician changes must be pre-approved and reassigned via the Field Nation application.*

Scope of Work DetailsEquipment Required:

- Analog Phone and/or Butt Set for call monitoring
- 66/110 Punch down tool and Cable Tester/Toner
- Cell phone with photo capability
- Permanent Marker with fine tip or labeler
- Telephone wire and connectors
- Drill and tools for mounting equipment
- Screws and/or washers for mounting the enclosure to the backboard
- Cellular Signal application for Signal/Speedtest

On-Site Tasks:Check-In:

- Use the Field Nation application to check in.

Customer Contact:

- Meet with the customer contact to identify MPOE or Telco rooms and phone equipment locations.

Call Bridge:

- Call the provided bridge call number for verbal instructions from MACH Activations. Alternate Technical Support number: 1-866-972-7677 x4.

Locate MPOE:

- Locate space in the MPOE to install the 2x2 enclosure and 66-block with a dedicated power outlet within 6 feet.

Photographs:

- Take photos of the mounting area and upload to Field Nation.

Panel Test Mode:

- *VERIFY WITH SITE THAT THE ALARM PANEL IS IN TEST.*

Power On:

- Power on the enclosure and inform MACH Activations for signal reading and Speed Test. Adjust the enclosure location based on signal readings if needed.

Locate CPE:

- Locate CPE (FACP, Elevators, Intercom, etc.) and take photos. Upload to Field Nation.

Verify Previous Lines:

- Check for dial tone (DT) and verify inbound/outbound calling functionality. For Fire lines, locate RJ31X jacks.

Tone, Trace, Tag:

- Tone, trace, and tag all POTS lines associated with the CPE. Provide TNs.

Identify Faults:

- Verify CPE functionality and identify any faults in Inside Wire (IW). Notify MACH Activations if faults are found.

Test Alarm Panels:

- Ensure alarm panels are in Normal Status. For Elevator lines, test cab buttons for proper call-out functionality. Confirm with MACH Activations.

Test Mode:

- Place FACP into Test Mode with customer assistance. Confirm with MACH Activations.

Cross-Connect Lines:

- Cross-connect customer existing lines to the MACH 66-block.

Conduct Testing:

- Test the Fire Lines to the Monitoring Company and verify with MACH Activations.

After Photos:

- Take after photos of the entire area and upload to Field Nation.

Check-Out:

- Check out of Field Nation, close the work order, and add closing notes.

Reporting:- Report any installation issues or anomalies in Field Nation.
- Update records to indicate a clean installation.
- Ensure the space is cleaned up and left neat.

Additional Note:

Please include all travel, tolls, and parking expenses in your counteroffer when requesting assignment. All requests for such will not be approved after assignment.

1. Confirm the start date and time. You will receive pre-calls at 24 hours and 2 hours prior to your ETA. If you do not answer or reply, you may lose the work as confirmation is a contractual obligation and a cancellation fee will not be granted
2. Confirm you have read this work order.

On-Site Tasks:

1. Check In Requirements- Follow in order
2. CHECK IN TO YOUR WORK ORDER–if you are unable to do so then you MUST call Essintial @ 855-612-2183 to check in.
3. CHECK IN with Manager/POC- Technician will introduce themselves to the MOD as the Essintial technician on behalf of Travel Center onsite for the De-installation.
4. Locate Packing materials shipped by customer and confirm you have the correct amount.
5. Locate Patch Cable sent by Essintial.
6. If you are unable to locate Packing materials or Patch Cables please check with the MOD.
7. Start the De - installation.PLEASE HAVE SITE MANAGEMENT CONFRIM THE EQUIPMENT YOU ARE TO DE-INSTALL

14. Use All Provided Materials: Ensure that all boxes, bubble wrap, and air pads are utilized for maximum equipment protection.
15. Packing materials will come with instructions as to how they are to be used.
16. Avoid Overpacking: Please avoid overstuffing boxes, as this could lead to damage during transport.
17. Secure Packing: All items must be securely packed and cushioned to prevent movement within the boxes.
18. Please ensure that monitors and pin pads are not placed screen down in the boxes to avoid damage. Always position them upright with adequate cushioning to protect screens during transit.
19. Ensure that each piece of equipment is adequately protected from potential impacts during travel.
20. Transport Considerations:Take extra care in preparing equipment for transit, as it will travel via ground in the back of a semi-truck. Proper packing is critical to avoid any damage.

Overview:

Seeking a technician with experience in network equipment installation and configuration.

Tech is required to install a Lumen 5G Router.

Estimated duration will be 45 minutes - 1 Hour

Dress Code:

Business Casual

Tools Required:

Basic Hand Tools

Laptop with ethernet cable

Zip Ties

Ladder

Tools required to run antenna cable.

Assorted Hardware for mounting the antenna to different surfaces. Brackets are supplied with the device.

Scope of Work:

Pre-Site Requirements

 Please review attached installation guide material prior to arriving on-site.

 Print off the 10T Solutions Acceptance Form.

Confirm WO and set start time 48 hours prior.

On-Site Tasks

Check-in to work order and introduce yourself to the onsite contact. You represent 10T Solutions on behalf of LUMEN while onsite.

 Assembly

Connect all 4 antennas.

Location for Mounting

Place the router high in the room (shelf or wall mount). Location of the device will have the greatest effect on performance. Try to mount as high as possible on a wall. Choosing an outside wall is usually a better choice. Mounting inside a metal rack will have a negative effect on performance. If the LCON says that it must be in a specific location document on the acceptance sheet and locate as instructed.

Power on

Connect Power Source

May take up to 5 minutes for initial scan and connection.

Connection LED (globe) will turn solid when complete.

 Network Connections

You will not make any connections to customer equipment. Any connections via LAN will be made by the customer.

If the customer has provided a cable for internet backup, connect an existing internet to the WAN 1 port.

WiFi can be enabled by request to Lumen or 10T Solutions support at 805-900-0809.

Test network connectivity and conduct a speed test.

Speed Test: The minimum required speed tests result is10/2 however if speeds are below 30/5 please evaluate location of router to determine if a different location will enhance performance. If speeds are still below minimum evaluate the site for an external antenna and call 10T support at 805-900-0809. Document recommendation in the "Speed Test - Antenna Evaluation info:" section of the 10T Acceptance Report.

Required On-Site Deliverables

All Deliverables must be uploaded immediately upon completion before leaving site.

Upload before and after photos of router and antenna.

Upload Cellular Speed Test Screenshot

Complete and upload 10T Solutions Acceptance Report.

Check-out and close work order

Escalation Process:

If any issue with the installation arises, call the 10T EWAS Escalation Support Hotline immediately 805-900-0809.

Support line is available between 9-5 pm EST at 805-900-0809 for Activation Assistance.

If clarification is needed on work order, contact support at 805-900-0809.

Speed Test below 30/5. Contact support at 805-900-0809.

Additional Hours & Expenses Approval Payment Policy

 Any additional hours or expenses need to be pre-approved prior to incurring on the work order.

Site/Customer: 

 

  

  

   

Dress Code:

- Professional work attire; closed-toe shoes and a safety vest may be required.

Materials/Tools Required:

Technician must arrive with:

- CAT5 wire
- 12-16 foot ladder
- Wiring fishing sticks
- Basic electrical hand tools
- Screwdrivers / terminal tools
- Multimeter
- Phone/camera for documentation

Materials shipping to site:

Phoenix Connector

Pre-Site Requirements:

- Schedule Confirmation: You must confirm the scheduled date and time frame with the project manager before arriving on-site to ensure Support Staff availability.
- Review FULL SOW.
- Review the training video attached to the client documents section of the WO.
- Reference Case: Keep Case available for all communications.

Scope of Work:

Check-In Requirements

Contact GridPoint Support upon arrival

 

 

- Check in with GridPoint Support upon arrival.
- Check out with GridPoint Support before leaving the site.

 1. Troubleshoot PowerlinkG3 Communications

Technician must:

- Work with GridPoint Support and TOC Lighting (866-798-6047 Option 3) to troubleshoot and restore communications to the PowerlinkG3 Lighting Panel.
- Verify all communication wiring and connections.
- Inspect the communication path between the PowerlinkG3 panel and the communication hub.
- Work with Support to clear panel memory as directed.

2. Repair or Replace Communication Wiring

Technician must:

- Test all communication cabling.
- Repair or replace damaged communication wiring as needed.
- Provide CAT5 wire.
- Be prepared to run new communication wiring from the PowerlinkG3 Lighting Panel to the communication hub.
- Use fishing sticks as needed to route new wiring.
- Provide photos of any wiring repairs or replacements.

3. Replace Phoenix Connector if Needed

Technician must:

- Inspect the existing Phoenix connector.
- Replace the Phoenix connector if found to be damaged or defective.
- Use the replacement part that was shipped to the store.
- Verify all wiring terminations are secure after replacement.
- Provide photos of the replacement installation.

4. Verify Lighting Control

Technician must:

- Verify communications have been restored.
- Test lighting operation with GridPoint Support and TOC Lighting.
- Confirm proper lighting control and panel functionality.
- Report any remaining issues before leaving the site.

- Phone with Camera

- Interface for connecting to remote servers such as puTTy on a computer.

- Must have a valid form of identification (Driver's license, Military ID, etc.)

On Site Appearance and Conduct: ZERO TOLERANCE

- Dress with the intention of being seen by the customer. Close toed shoes, business casual, khakis, jeans, and a collared shirt are required. Khaki/jeans pants and shirts are expected to be clean and without holes. No company logos or print. No hats.
- Always be respectful, professional and courteous with the end-user. All communication with the end user shall be in conjunction with the current SOW. All other communication is forbidden. Tech is not to communicate with any site contacts in regards to scheduling or pay, only contact your helpdesk representative. Tech is not to mention Fieldnation to end users In any shape or form.
- In the event of a potential issue onsite, you are to remove yourself from the site to avoid confrontation and contact your helpdesk representative immediately to discuss the next steps in coming up with a resolution.
- Disrespect or failure to uphold our company image to the customer will not be tolerated. It will result in a cancelation with zero compensation and the loss of any future opportunities with our company.

SCHEDULING & ARRIVAL:

- TEAMSOS operates on a Hard Start schedule to ensure the best possible service experience for our customers.
- We do not permit Rescheduling or Cancellations, but if/when it’s required: Techs must contact TEAMSOS to request at least 48 hrs. in advance of the work order date and time via Support at 916-577-1774.
- Check-in/Check-out must be completed while onsite. If installation cannot start or be completed for any reason, you must garner TEAMSOS approval prior to exiting site.
- If you arrive “late”: Your arrival time will not be adjusted, and when past Field Nation’s 15-minute grace period will impact your timeliness rating. We will not take calls requesting arrival time overrides, so please plan accordingly.
- Please note there are penalties associated with arriving late, and checking in/out off-site.

19835039.d:
What is a Property IT Takeover?

An IT takeover is part of the onboarding process when assuming responsibility for a property's technology environment. As an onsite tech, you’ll work closely with a remote technician to:

- Set up and configure leasing office computers
- Connect systems to the office network
- Assist with scan-to-email functionality on printers
- Deliver and collect a property questionnaire
- Take documentation photos and upload them to SharePoint

This work is hands-on and collaborative, with most tasks performed in real-time alongside your assigned remote tech.

MUST-KNOW BEFORE ACCEPTING – READ THIS FIRST

We do not typically reimburse expenses. The compensation listed in the work order covers both labor and travel.

However, we may make exceptions for materials only (e.g., USB drives, cabling, etc.) and for parking costs if they are needed on a case-by-case basis and only with prior approval. We do not reimburse for the following:

- Travel (gas, mileage, hotel, airfare, etc.)
- Tolls
- Meals or lunch breaks
- Cleanup/setup time

You are only paid for time working with the remote technician. Time is cross-referenced via timestamped logs.

Punctuality is Critical:

- If you are 20+ minutes late, the work order may be canceled.
- Early arrival does not qualify for extra pay — payment starts when work begins.
- Lunch breaks are not paid and must be communicated to the remote tech at check-in.

Schedule Flexibility Required:

- Appointment times are based on the client’s schedule.
- Work dates may change frequently and at the last minute.
- By accepting this work order, you agree to accommodate those changes.

ON THE DAY OF SERVICE – WHAT TO EXPECT

Upon Arrival:

- Go inside the leasing office and check in with the staff.
- Immediately call your assigned remote technician.
- Ask the onsite staff if any network equipment is managed by a third party. If yes, notify your remote tech right away.

During the Visit:

- Follow your remote tech’s instructions.
- There will be minimal downtime — expect to be working throughout.
- Do not complete additional requests from property staff unless approved by the remote tech.

Upon Completion:

- Check out with the leasing staff.
- Call the remote tech to officially close out the visit.

WHAT TO BRING – REQUIRED EQUIPMENT

Arrive fully prepared with:

- Laptop (Windows preferred) with charger and Ethernet port (or adapter)
- 6-foot or longer Cat5e/Cat6 Ethernet cable
- Two USB drives (8GB or larger):
- One with Windows 11 installer
- One with Hiren’s BootCD --> <https://www.hirensbootcd.org/usb-booting/>
- Smartphone:
- Must take photos in JPEG format (HEIC is not accepted)
- Fully charged with a charger

REQUIRED SKILLS & EXPECTATIONS

Technicians must have:

- Proficiency with Windows OS setup and reinstallation
- Familiarity with basic networking (subnets, connections)
- Ability to install/uninstall software
- Understanding of boot menu options
- Strong time management and punctuality

WORK SCOPE – WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

General Overview:

- Check in with leasing office and remote tech
- Assist in setting up computers and connecting to the network
- Test printer scan-to-email functionality
- Deliver and collect the property questionnaire
- Take documentation photos and upload to SharePoint
- Complete other onboarding tasks as directed by the remote tech

Out of Scope:

- Factory resetting or replacing equipment without approval
- General troubleshooting not assigned
- Any tasks requested by property staff that aren’t in the work order or directed by the remote tech

ADDITIONAL NOTE FOR COMPANIES DISPATCHING TECHNICIANS

If you are a dispatching company, you must provide the personal Field Nation profile of the technician who will be onsite.

If a different person is sent than the one submitted, the work order may be canceled and you may be removed from future opportunities.

Technicians are selected based on their individual skills and reviews.

Tools: Smart Phone with charger, hotspot, wifi and camera capable and Standard tool kit with Phillips and Flathead screwdrivers (multiple sizes), box cutter, flash light

Penalties/Deductions:

10% Deduction for 15 minutes or more late.

10% Deduction for being unprepared.

Tech swaps MUST be approved in advance. Failure to do so will result in no pay of WO.

Unauthorized assistants are prohibited from all Insight work. Those assistants will be asked to leave and wait offsite for you to complete the job.

Terms for Travel:

Payment amount listed on this WO is an all-in rate

If provider is seeking additional compensation for travel time due to distance from work order, this must be requested as a counter-offer PRIOR to assignment

If submitted post-assignment, pay increase requests for travel time will not be approved

Tolls or Parking fees will only be eligible for reimbursement if receipt is attached to the work order when closed out

Terms for Additional Time Required Onsite:

Technician must call buyer contact listed in WO immediately upon realizing additional time over max hours in WO will be required

If additional time required is due to factors agreed to by buyer as outside of tech control; technician may submit request for pay increase for time onsite over max in WO

 IMPORTANT: Pay increase for additional time must be requested and Approved by buyer while tech is onsite; additional time logged by tech on WO or pay increase requests will only be paid if tech obtained pre-approval from buyer POC while onsite

Tech must enter name of buyer contact who approved increase to ensure any approval questions are directed accordingly

*The job is considered incomplete if you leave site before sending any required deliverables and calling Insight Command Center to check out, which will cause a delay in pay or no compensation*

Scope: Remove 37 hard drives from 2 servers and document each drive. Inventory all servers and any other serialized devices, recording serial numbers, makes, models, device types, and asset tags. Note the parent-child relationship between each drive and its source device.

Work Order Requirements:

1)  Technicians:

- Must be background-checked and drug-screened within the last 24 months.
- Must have the specified tools and equipment.
- Must check in and out using GPS.
- Must communicate clearly via the platform.

2) Required Tools and Equipment:

- Laptop with MS Excel.
- 1D/2D barcode scanner (no scanner apps).
- Tools for removing servers in a data center.
- Power screwdriver with various screwdriver bits.

On-site Safety:

- Follow general data center safety precautions.
- Do not disconnect or connect hardwired connections of rack's PDUs, UPS modules, tape libraries, or other computer equipment.
- Disconnect equipment cautiously from pluggable AC receptacles.
- Refer to Policies and Procedures for more information.

Code of Conduct:

- Be punctual and courteous.
- Avoid personal calls and texting while working.
- Do not discuss payment details or offer services to the client.

Dress Code:

- No graphic tops.
- Clean and unripped jeans or khakis.
- Clean shoes (no open-toed shoes or sandals).
- No shorts.
- Polo or button-down shirt preferred.

Expenses and Budgets:

- Parking reimbursement with receipt.
- Other expenses require approval. Over-budget items require approval before the work is completed.

Detailed Scope of Work:

- Inventory all assets, capturing serial numbers, asset tags, make, model, and device types.
- Remove hard disks and establish parent-child relationships using the provided spreadsheet. Scan the HDD’s serial number into the Serial # field and the device’s serial number into the Parent S/N field, linking the HDD to the parent device.
- Stage hard disks for shredding and devices for pickup.
- Clean up the work area.

Escalations On-site:

- Contact the work order manager with any questions or concerns.
- If you are asked to perform other services or if the scope of work differs from the work order, contact the work order manager.

MAIN COMPONENTS IN OUR CLIENT'S SYSTEM

- Samsung, Sony, and LG displays. We use Samsung in a majority of our installs​. Most of the Samsung displays are SSP displays and get their content from the internet. You will often find that unplugging the power cord will fix most issues. This is considered a hard reset. Most techs will just perform a soft reset and the problem wont go away. A soft reset is just turning off the display by the power button.
- HDBaseT equipment. On our older installs we use Monoprice. Newer installs you will find CableTronix or Atlona equipment. With the exception of Atlona we used a splitter to transmit the signal over ethernet. Atlona is an all in one solution (splitter, POE, Transmitter)
- Episode and Ashley amps. We have a standard that Input 1 is the in store/branch channel. Input 2 is reserved for outdoor audio.
- Media players - In some locations you will find two Seneca players. 1 is for the Digital Signage and 1 is for the radio. You can easily find the radio player by ensuring that it does not have an HDMI cable installed. Our radio players do not need an HDMI cable. You will also find other models. All models should be identified with a Revel sticker on the bottom. Sometimes our clients will put their own asset labels on the equipment so do get discouraged if you can't find the player. Call tech support if you can't find a player​

Important Component Information

Most of the components are in the IT/Network room. We do have some players behind Displays. If you can not find the media players contact Revel immediately.

EQUIPMENT THAT YOU ARE REQUIRED TO HAVE

Keyboard and Mouse - Wireless is preferred but corded will work. There are times that you will need to access the network screen to see if the device is hooked up to the internet and to install Teamviewer if it is not installed.

USB Splitter - Some of our media players have limited USB connections.

Monitor that has HDMI inputs. We have some models that have VGA outputs but you will need a VGA cord.

Network Cable Tester: All of our clients use network for their service. Sometimes the network cables go bad so as a last resort you will be asked to check pairing and continuity

Receptacle Tester: Sometimes you will have components that will not turn on and the LED lights aren't on so you will need to check the outlet to eliminate electrical issues.

Ladder: A frame ladder that will get to 8'. Do not use ladders that will need to leaned up against the wall.

Camera: You will be asked to upload pictures of the displays and components to verify that the issue was fixed.

Phone: You will need to contact Revel Tech Support before you leave the clients location. There are no exceptions. You have been given several contact numbers to call.

- Snips  
- Smartphone with Microsoft Teams mobile app  
- Tone generator with probe  
- Data cabling tester (must say "Pass" / "Fail")  
- Punch down tool with a 110-blade  
  
DRESS CODE  
- Polo shirt  
- Jeans or khaki pants (no shorts)

- Only confirmed technicians are authorized to be on-site for an activity/dispatch.  
- Any scheduling or tech assignment requests/changes must receive prior approval.  
- Furthermore, additional technicians and/or supervisors are not authorized to accompany assigned tech(s) onsite at any time without prior approval.

- Technician will ensure no other circuit is connected to this device.

- Device will be packed for shipment
- Technician MUST take pictures of device wrapped in bubble wrap and placed in the shipping box.
- Pictures must be attached to assignment for payment approval
- Once packed appropriately and pictures taken technician will provide box to store management to ship back to Verizon
- Technician must get sign off on the assignment from the member of store management that equipment to be shipped back has been provided to

Scope of Work:

Make sure to be on time as we have a 4-hour window for install/cutover

FE will be working with the tech app link and ServicePoint TAC support.

Link will be in your custom fields

1.Arrival & Check-In

- Upon arrival, check in using the TECH APP (link will be provided). Call into ServicePoint TAC at 973-334-5052 Option 2 to check in as well.
- If access issues occur, immediately contact the Service Point TAC.

2.New Equipment Verification

- Tech will receive a box of new MetTel equipment from the POC.
- Take clear photos of all new equipment.
- Text photos to TECH APP.

3.Existing Equipment Documentation

- Take photos of all existing mounted equipment and upload to TECH APP
- See if you can remove the old equipment backboard without disconnecting any lines
- ⚠️TECH MUST NOT TAKE THE SITE DOWN UNLESS DIRECTED BY SERVICE POINT. So be careful with the existing equipment.

4.Line & Port Identification

- Identify all existing phone numbers on the 66-block and label them.
- Identify and label all existing connections on the Velo.

5.Continue following the TECH APP directions for staging and cutover. IF you have any issues, call into ServicePoint TAC for support.

Reminder again. DO NOT TAKE THE SITE DOWN UNLESS DIRECTED BY SERVICE POINT

- After staging is done and new equipment is powered on call ServicePoint TAC so they can confirm status of the PIAB.
- Once they confirm everything is good, they will instruct you to proceed with cutover.
- Once cutover is complete you will call back to ServicePoint TAC for confirmation that everything is up and running.
- Ask MOD to test the site as well.

6.After confirmation the site is up and good, you will then proceed to decommission the old equipment and take pictures of those serial numbers. You will upload those pictures to the TECH APP as well.

- Place equipment in the box the new equipment arrived in.
- Attach provided return label.
- Take a photo and hand the boxed equipment to the Manager on Duty.

7.Call ServicePoint for release

- After you get confirmation that everything is good confirm that the TECH APP is fully completed as well.
- Tech MUST NOT leave site before confirming being released by a ServicePoint TAC Member and having the Tech app filled completed.

REQUIRED SKILLS: Mid-level to advanced-level network tech. Must be able to run cable neatly through various ceiling types, terminate cables with RJ45 plugs and or Keystone jacks. Must be able to Operate a Lift.

OVERVIEW:

- Scope Of Work: Technician needed onsite to install new customer provided APs or move existing APs, run cable as necessary, and provide additional troubleshooting. While onsite and after completing the install and cable run, tech MUST complete capture various photos and complete the Essintial Online Deliverable Survey using the provided link. Once all tasks are completed, the technician will contact the Essintial Technical Support @ 717-516-3009 to validate that the data capture is completed, review the completed online deliverable and obtain approval prior to leaving the site.
- Technicians will need to complete multiple wifi surveys onsite - one in the Service Bay(s) and one in the Service Plaza

Engagement: Long-Term (12 Months) | 8 hours | 2 days WEEKEND WORK ONLY

Why this opportunity?

Are you ready to elevate your IT Support expertise? We’re looking for an Entry-Level Field Inspection Technician to support a new customer to the FN platform. This isn't just a gig—it’s stable, long-term work that puts a top-tier name on your resume.

Consistent income: 8 hours each weekend for approximately 12 months. W2 benefit: As a W2 employee, the standard10% Field Nation platform fee doesn’t apply. You keep 100% of your hourly rate (before taxes).

Full support: You will be hired as a W2 employee through our trusted Employer of Record (EOR), granting you access to a benefits package including health, 401k, Worker's Comp, and sick time (if applicable), provided you meet eligibility requirements.

Pay & Schedule

Rate: $37/hour

Schedule: 4 hours each weekend day (approximately 12 months in length)

Hours - 9:00 AM - 1:00 PM, Saturday & Sunday

Scope of Work:

Entry-Level Field Inspection Technician - The objective of this role is to establish a consistent daily onsite presence to perform routine visual inspections and operational checks. Resource serves as the “eyes and ears” onsite, helping ensure operational uptime while providing proactive reporting back to the customer support team.

About This Role:

On-Site Visual Inspection & Reporting of EV Charging Stations

Resource Requirements

- Entry-level / Junior Technician

Desired Attributes

- Reliable and punctual
- Comfortable following digital checklists
- Strong communication skills through Slack / mobile applications

Tools / PPE

- Experience using multi-meters and have basic knowledge of hand tools
- Standard PPE required
- Specialized repair tools are not required initially
- If advanced repair work is needed, tools will be shipped onsite or a higher-tier technician will be dispatched separately, role will perform basic, non-complex inspections of site equipment.

Key Responsibilities

- Daily visual inspections of chargers, power units, and related equipment
- Monitor and report fuel / consumable levels
- Provide live updates through a designated Slack channel
- Perform basic guided troubleshooting directed by remote support
- Escalate issues requiring specialized repair or support

Communication & Support

- Technician will have access to live support from the customer’s internal operations team
- Documentation, check-in/check-out, and work tracking will be managed through the Field Nation platform
- Real-time updates and findings will be communicated through Slack

Next Steps

Qualified candidates will be contacted for a phone screening and buyer interview. Selected candidates will then complete W2 onboarding through the Employer of Record. As a part of the process the EOR requires a secondary Field Nation ID to be created that will only be tied to the EOR.

Testing TESTING REQUIREMENTS

• All new cables MUST have a certified passing test result.

 Note 1: Certifiers must meet TIA-1152 and IEC 61935-1, and to be UL or ETL verified for applicable level

Tester Set up for Cat6a copper cable.

b. The Manufacturer and part number info is on the cable jacket.

5. Connector Type: RJ45 - 8p8c
